eyebrow: Quantum Error Correction & Fault Tolerance · Chapter 3
subtitle: Lesson 13 · Quantum Error Correction Basics

steps.label: 1. Prepare a fresh ancilla qubit in |0⟩
steps.sub: An intermediary, never one of the data qubits

steps.label: 2-3. CNOT from data qubit 1, then data qubit 2, onto the ancilla
steps.sub: Entangling the ancilla with the two qubits being compared

steps.label: 4. Measure the ancilla in the Z basis
steps.sub: Agree -> the two CNOTs cancel, ancilla reads 0; disagree -> ancilla reads 1

steps.label: That measured bit IS the Z1Z2 syndrome bit
steps.sub: A second ancilla, wired to qubits 2 and 3, gives the Z2Z3 bit the same way

eyebrow: Why this doesn't reveal the data

steps.label: The ancilla only learns 'do qubits 1 and 2 agree'
steps.sub: Never the actual superposition amplitudes α and β

steps.label: Z1Z2 gives the same +1 eigenvalue on both logical states
steps.sub: So it can't distinguish 'which logical state is this' — can't collapse the superposition

steps.label: This is the concrete resolution to Chapter 2's puzzle
steps.sub: Real quantum measurement, zero disturbance to α|0⟩_L + β|1⟩_L

steps.label: No-cloning is never violated
steps.sub: Nothing about α or β is ever copied or revealed — only agreement/disagreement

eyebrow: Generalizes to every code — and the catch

steps.label: The Steane code and surface code use this exact pattern
steps.sub: More stabilizers, more ancillas, different wiring — same primitive

steps.label: The surface code (Chapter 5) does this in parallel, across a grid
The catch: the ancilla itself can be faulty
steps.sub: Its prep, CNOTs, and measurement are imperfect physical operations too

steps.label: A faulty round can report the wrong syndrome
steps.sub: Fault-tolerant protocols (Chapter 7) repeat extraction to tell real errors from faulty rounds

subtitle: Trace both 3-qubit codes by hand, end to end, before moving to the stabilizer formalism.
